name: Email to matter
summary: Takes a client email to the right matter in Smokeball: matches the sender to an open matter (or opens a lead for an unknown sender when the firm allows it), records a note and a follow-up task, and queues any reply to the client's portal for approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every message that reaches a client.

covered_by.triage: intake (one open matter) or a person
covered_by.reply-client: reply (queued portal message after a person writes it)

covered_by.new-matter-open: intake (lead matter for an unknown sender, when lead_matter_type_id is set)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Match each new email's sender to an open matter, or open a lead matter when the firm allows it. Unclear senders wait for a person.

crons.name: file
crons.summary: Read the matter's recent notes for context, then record a note of the email and a follow-up task on the matter.

crons.name: reply
crons.summary: Queue each written reply as a Smokeball portal message to the client, for a person to approve.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations are reads, and writes that reach nobody outside the firm: a lead matter that a person has not yet opened, a note on a matter, a follow-up task. The one message to a client, a portal message, is a live operation and is only ever queued for a person to approve.

smokeball.covers: sender lookup, open matters, lead matter, matter notes and recent notes, follow-up task, portal reply (queued for approval)

gaps: No inbox reader: Smokeball's API does not read Outlook. Emails arrive through the Smokeball Outlook add-in or a person, who records them in the workflow store (collection emails). A Microsoft 365 mail reader is needed before intake runs by itself.
The email itself (body and attachments) is not filed into the matter's documents. The Outlook add-in does that. AddFile is mapped but creates a file record without the content, so it is not used.
Replies go to the client's Smokeball portal only. Smokeball's API has no email send, so a client without portal access gets no reply from this workflow.
Writing the reply is judgment. The agent skill writes it after reading the stored notes for the matter, and never sends it.
Triage is partial: the add-in suggests matters, but its suggestions are not in the API. This workflow matches only by sender address and only when there is exactly one open matter.

Sender matching relies on GetContacts with the email address as Search. A live account must confirm that Search matches email addresses and that the contact response returns them. A contact is matched only when its own email field equals the sender, and the spec does not type that field: until a live account shows its name, no contact matches and every sender is treated as unknown (fails closed).

Cron logs: the runtime writes each queued approval's summary, which names the sender address, to the cron log. Keeping the address out of logs needs a change in core/workflows/runtime.ts (log the approval id only). The draft-side summaries already carry email and matter ids only.
Creating a lead for a new sender needs lead_matter_type_id. A lead saved with no client attached is not confirmed. New contacts are not created here.
A crash between creating a lead matter and saving its id can repeat the lead. Check the matter list after such a crash.
Conflict checks: the Smokeball pages describe none, and no operation is mapped. This stays with the firm.
Deadlines and court dates: no calendar event is created here. The follow-up task is the only diary entry.
Actionstep: its docs were read but the kit has no Actionstep operations, so it is not mapped. LEAP has no kit platform and no docs were read for it.
Smokeball is spec-only: the operations come from the vendor OpenAPI file and are tested offline. Every adapter stays docs-only until a Smokeball sandbox or trial account proves it.
Capability keys: core/capabilities.json has no key for creating a matter or a memo, so those writes are described here only.
